title: Minimax Testing for Constancy of the True-Propensity Effect Curve
banked_reason: D0.5 mathematical and decision panels pass with verified citations, but the cold novelty referee assigns subfield below the field floor, paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4 and salvageable=false; independent validity review confirms sound restricted-class rates with no bounded same-question route to field.
gap_reasons: The significance is limited by the known uniform two-dimensional design, fixed smoothness balls, and global horizontal submersion, with no achieved upper theorem outside that setting
The all-sample guarantee supplies no useful practical calibration: the specified tests accept automatically below 2^2048, and the advertised upper separations there have empty alternatives
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery closed the matched unknown-score n^(-4/13) and sampled-score n^(-4/9) testing rates on the fixed primitive class; both substantive panels passed and both cited leaves were verified. The independent terminal-validity review confirmed sound NL arguments, but the cold review capped the contribution at subfield because of the restrictive design/submersion assumptions and automatic acceptance below 2^2048. The operator field-floor rule stopped the run before Lean formalization; there is no Lean proof or formal substrate to promote.
tldr: Constancy of the causal true-propensity curve allows substantial within-score effect heterogeneity. On this note's fixed binary uniform-design primitive class, original-record minimax \(L_2(J_0)\) separation is \(n^{-4/13}\). Supplying only the exact true propensity value attached to each observed record gives \(n^{-4/9}\), with both outcome means still unknown. Explicit finite tests and original Bernoulli mixtures certify the same all-sample constants, no logarithmic loss, and a vanishing radius ratio. This is a restricted calibration benchmark, not an upper theorem for the broader published classes.
gap: Dai, Shen and Stern (2023) provide asymptotic propensity-weighted tests across prespecified strata; Xie, Brand and Jann (2012) study propensity-indexed treatment effects. Neither supplies whole-primitive-class finite-sample minimax L2 separation for constancy of the smooth true-propensity curve with the score learned from the same original binary records. Pointwise estimated-covariate regression and generated-regressor specification results also do not supply that theorem.
fill: A moving-fiber original-likelihood converse, total finite-data calibration and a matched revealed-score benchmark jointly target \(r_n^{*,\mathrm{rev}}/r_n^*\to0\). Exact rate powers, logarithms, all-sample constants and any quantitative crossover remain open obligations.
